Photograph: AFP/Getty Images Russia Moscow threat of ‘consequences’ will not alter UK support for Ukraine, says Burnham Prime minister responds to Russian anger over Kyiv’s use of British-made drones in ‘deep strike’ campaign UK politics live – latest updates Europe live – latest updates Jamie Grierson and Rowena Mason Tue 18 Aug 2026 08.13 EDT First published on Tue 18 Aug 2026 03.27 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Andy Burnham says the UK will continue to “support Ukraine 100%” after Russia threatened consequences after strikes by British-made drones. The Russian embassy to the UK said on Monday that Britain had been deliberately escalating the Ukraine conflict and the deeper its involvement, “the higher the price it will pay”. Burnham, asked during a visit to Wolverhampton on Tuesday for his response to Moscow’s threat, said: “This is the UK doing what it has long said it would do, which is to support Ukraine 100% against this illegal war led by Vladimir Putin. “We are providing support so that Ukraine can defend itself, and that’s been the British position all the way through this conflict by previous prime ministers. It remains the case with me. We are not fair-weather friends. We will be there in Ukraine’s hour of need, and that won’t change.” The use of the drones made by UK companies is part of Ukraine’s “deep strike” campaign. However, it is not the first time Ukraine has deployed British-made equipment in Russia, having long used Storm Shadow missiles. Kyiv has stepped up its attacks this year, with long-range missiles and swarms of drones increasingly targeting Russia’s military industries and energy facilities. chart It has also hit large depots of Russia’s largest online retailer, Wildberries, burning merchandise worth billions of pounds and bringing the war home to the Russian public more than four years into Moscow’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine. Russia’s embassy to the UK said on Monday that the reports confirmed that “London is deliberately opting for an escalation of the Ukraine crisis”, accusing Britain of “seeking to contain Russia and inflict maximum damage on it by proxy”. “London’s actions will inevitably carry consequences for which it will have to answer,” it said. “The deeper its involvement in the conflict and the greater its support for Kyiv’s terrorist machinery, the higher the price it will pay.” skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to First Edition Our morning email breaks down the key stories of the day, telling you what’s happening and why it matters after newsletter promotion Ukraine war briefing: Russian campaign to ‘weaponise winter’ under way Read more A Ministry of Defence spokesperson said: “Britain stands shoulder to shoulder with Ukraine and we are committed to providing the equipment Ukraine needs to defend itself against Putin’s illegal invasion. Russia should be in no doubt about the resolve of this government to stand against Russian aggression, in Ukraine and against the UK and our allies.” Ukraine’s strategy of long-range drone strikes is thought to be intended to cut Moscow’s revenue for the war and to make Russian civilians feel the impact of the invasion. Kyiv launched three times as many such strikes in July as it did in January, according to data from Acled, an independent conflict monitor. Repeatedly hitting deep into Russia has forced Moscow to stretch its air defences over a larger area. Russia’s defence ministry said on Saturday it had shot down 598 Ukrainian drones over 19 Russian regions as well as the Black Sea, the Azov Sea and the annexed Ukrainian peninsula of Crimea. Officials said on Monday that Ukrainian long-range attacks on Russia killed seven people overnight, while five civilians died in Ukraine after strikes by Moscow’s forces. Russian missile attacks on Tuesday killed ⁠10 ⁠people and injured ​eight ⁠in a village in ⁠Ukraine’s north-eastern ​Kharkiv ‌oblast, the ‌regional governor ‌said. The strike on the village of Pechenihy ‌damaged 10 private buildings, a ​cafe, a post office, a ⁠shop and ​at least ​seven cars, ​Oleh Syniehubov ​said ‌on ​Telegram. A rapid development of largely homegrown technologies, including the Flamingo cruise missile and the FP-1 long-range fixed-wing drone from Fire Point, have allowed Ukraine to bomb warehouses, oil refineries, ports and military facilities up to 1,500 miles (2,400km) from its border. Ukraine can now almost match the deep-strike capability Russia has had since the beginning of the war using large drones and cruise missiles, though it does not possess the high-speed ballistic missiles Moscow frequently uses. At the same time, both sides’ air defences are stretched to the point of near exhaustion, leading to an increase in civilian casualties and worries that the impact of the conflict beyond the immediate frontlines will only increase into the winter. https://www.dw.com/en/ukraine-russia-tra.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5MIhy Traffic through the Starokozace crossing between Ukraine and Moldova was halted Image: OdeskaODA/Telegram Advertisement A Ukrainian drone attack on the Black Sea port city of Novorossiysk overnight killed at least four people, including a child, Russian officials said Wednesday. Veniamin Kondratyev, the governor of the Krasnodar region in southern Russia , said 29 others were injured in the drone attack. Ukraine has frequently targeted Novorossiysk, a port city that is a major outlet for Russian oil and grain exports . Earlier on Wednesday, the mayor of the city, Andrei Kravchenko, had said the debris from a Ukrainian drone fell onto several businesses and nearly landed on a residential building, sparking fires. In the nearby town of Anapa, falling drone debris damaged three homes and a kindergarten, Kondratyev said, adding that there were no casualties. Russia's Defense Ministry said nearly 600 Ukrainian drones had been shot down overnight. Two civilians killed in Russian attack on border crossing Russian drone strikes overnight on a border crossing between Ukraine and Moldova, meanwhile, killed at least two civilians, the regional governor Oleh Kiper said on social media . Three people were wounded in the strike on the Starokozace border crossing, around 500 kilometres (310 miles) south of Kyiv, Ukraine's State Border Guard Service said. The strikes forced the checkpoint to close temporarily, Kiper said, adding that multiple fires broke out as a result of the attack. Ukrainian emergency officials also said the capital, Kyiv was attacked overnight. While some fires were started, there were no casualties. Russia's drone attack damaged a passenger bus and started fires, Ukraine said Image: OdeskaODA/Telegram What is the latest in US-brokered peace talks? Russia on Tuesday resumed its near-daily airstrikes on Kyiv after a brief pause while US negotiators Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner visited Moscow for talks. At least five people were killed in Kyiv on Tuesday, officials said. Russia also said President Vladimir Putin had had an "extremely frank" phone call with his US counterpart Donald Trump on Tuesday, as Washington continues to press Ukrainian and Russian officials to hold face-to-face talks to end the war . Ukraine has suggested talks that could take place in September, but Russian officials have said it is "too early" to discuss specifics such as a venue or dates for the talks. Despite US pressure, talks between Moscow and Kyiv have yielded no results beyond sporadic prisoner swaps. https://www.theguardian.com/world/video/.text: 0:50 Spain People and pets rescued by helicopter from floods in Spain – video Helicopters rescued people stranded on rooftops as torrential rain swept across eastern Spain on Monday. Floods and storms killed at least four people, and shelter-in-place orders remained in force for more than 80,000 people. The downpour from Storm Adam cut off several towns along the Mediterranean coast as rivers overflowed their banks and streets turned into rivers. More than 2,000 people were evacuated, mainly in Oliva, and authorities carried out nearly 496 rescues in Valencia and Alicante, the Civil Guard police said Source: Reuters Tue 20 Oct 2026 10.09 EDT Last modified on Tue 20 Oct 2026 10.52 EDT Share Explore more on these topics Spain Flooding Europe weather Europe Most viewed Most viewed World Europe US news Americas Asia Australia Middle East Africa Inequality Global development
